I am a first-year PhD student in Health Policy at Harvard University, on the
economics track.

I study health insurance markets and the regulations that shape them — how
insurers respond to capital requirements, how prices are set and disclosed, and
what these mechanisms mean for the cost and availability of coverage.

Before starting at Harvard I spent two years as a research assistant at the
**Federal Reserve Board**, in the Flow of Funds section, working with Board
economists on projects spanning insurance pricing, bank lending, and household
outcomes. Earlier I worked at the **Hilltop Institute** on hospital price
transparency, assembling newly public pricing data across 31 states. I hold a BA
in Economics and Political Science from UMBC.

## Research interests

::: {.interests}
- Health insurance regulation — risk-based capital, reinsurance, medical loss ratios
- ACA exchanges and state reinsurance programs
- Hospital pricing and price transparency
- Medicaid and Medicare managed care
- Applied microeconometrics: bunching and kink designs, event studies
:::

See [Research](research.qmd) for more, or the [CV](cv.qmd) for the full record.
